A clearer starting point for an inherited home

Inheriting a home can bring a lot of questions at once. Should you keep it, rent it, or sell it? And what was the property actually worth when your loved one passed away? For families in Tucson and throughout Southern Arizona, an independent estate appraisal can help replace guesswork with a documented opinion of value.

Understanding retrospective value

An estate appraisal may require a retrospective valuation, meaning the appraiser develops an opinion of the property’s market value as of a date in the past, often the date of death. That figure may be useful for estate administration, discussions among heirs, and tax planning. A current online estimate is not a substitute for a properly developed retrospective appraisal, especially when the home has changed condition or the market has shifted.

Prepare the right records and valuation date

Before making decisions, gather any relevant estate documents, the property address, and information about improvements or repairs. Reddy Appraisal LLC provides independent residential valuation services in Tucson and Southern Arizona, including retrospective assignments when appropriate. Your estate attorney or tax professional can advise which valuation date and documentation your situation requires.
